tools.name: get_component_catalog
tools.summary: Returns every component type available in this Unity project.
tools.description:
Returns every component type available in this Unity project.

Includes built-in Unity components (Rigidbody, BoxCollider, Light, AudioSource,
Camera, NavMeshAgent, etc.) and user MonoBehaviour scripts from project assemblies.

For each component:
  type_name         — use as component_type_name in add_component_to_object
  display_name      — human-readable label
  category         — Physics | Rendering | Audio | Animation | Navigation |
                     Camera | Effects | UserScript | Physics2D
  source           — "BuiltIn" or "UserScript"
  script_path       — asset path for UserScript components, null for BuiltIn
  disallow_multiple — true if only one instance is allowed per GameObject
  properties[]     — serialized properties with:
    property_path   — EXACT key to use in add_component_to_object properties
    display_name    — Inspector label (e.g. "Mass", "Use Gravity")
    type           — Float | Integer | Boolean | String | Enum:Name[Val0|Val1]
                     | Vector2 | Vector3 | Color | ObjectReference:Type | etc.
    default_value   — C# default as a string (informational)
    enum_names[]    — valid enum value names (only present for Enum properties)

CRITICAL — property paths:
  For built-in components the serialized path is NOT the C# property name.
  The catalog gives you the exact internal path:
    Rigidbody.mass     → property_path "m_Mass"
    Light.intensity    → property_path "m_Intensity"
    Camera.fieldOfView → property_path "field of view"
  Always use property_path from this catalog — never guess.
  For user scripts, property_path matches the C# field name.

Call once per session and cache; only changes when new scripts are added.

tools.name: add_component_to_object
tools.summary:
Adds a component to a scene GameObject and sets its properties atomically.
The operation is registered with Unity's Undo system.
tools.description:
Adds a component to a scene GameObject and sets its properties atomically.
The operation is registered with Unity's Undo system.

WORKFLOW:
  1. Call get_component_catalog() to find the type and valid property paths.
  2. Call get_scene_hierarchy() if you need to confirm the object path.
  3. Call add_component_to_object() with the type and desired properties.

PROPERTY FORMAT:
  properties is a list of { "property_path": "...", "value": ... }.
  Use property_path exactly as returned by get_component_catalog.

  Value formats by type:
    Float, Integer  → number:         9.81
    Boolean         → boolean:        true
    String          → string:         "idle"
    Enum            → string:         "Continuous"  (use enum_names from catalog)
    Vector2         → array:          [1.0, 0.0]
    Vector3         → array:          [0.0, -9.81, 0.0]
    Color           → array [r,g,b,a]: [1.0, 0.5, 0.0, 1.0]  (0–1 range)
    Bounds          → array [cx,cy,cz,sx,sy,sz]: [0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2]
    Rect            → array [x,y,w,h]: [0, 0, 100, 50]
    LayerMask       → integer bitmask: 1
    ObjectReference → object: { "asset_guid": "abc123..." }

EXAMPLES:
  Add a Rigidbody with custom mass:
    object_path = "/Environment/Barrel"
    component_type_name = "Rigidbody"
    properties = [
      { "property_path": "m_Mass",       "value": 5.0   },
      { "property_path": "m_UseGravity",  "value": false }
    ]

  Add a warm point light:
    component_type_name = "Light"
    properties = [
      { "property_path": "m_Type",      "value": "Point"              },
      { "property_path": "m_Color",     "value": [1.0, 0.85, 0.6, 1.0] },
      { "property_path": "m_Intensity", "value": 2.0                  },
      { "property_path": "m_Range",     "value": 10.0                 }
    ]

object_path:          Hierarchy path, e.g. "/Player", "/Environment/Barrel"
component_type_name:  type_name from get_component_catalog
properties:           List of { property_path, value } (omit to keep defaults)
update_if_exists:     If true, update an existing component instead of erroring

tools.name: create_zone_scaffold
tools.summary: Creates a ScaffoldZone GameObject with auto-generated anchor points.
tools.description:
Creates a ScaffoldZone GameObject with auto-generated anchor points.

── ZONE TYPES ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SpiralStaircase  Descends on local -Y. Anchors: _entry (top), step_01…step_NN,
                 _mid, _exit (bottom). Required dims: width, step_count,
                 riser_height, turns.

StraightCorridor Extends on local +Z. Anchors: _entry, _exit, _mid, _quarter,
                 _three_quarter, _left_wall_mid, _right_wall_mid.
                 Required dims: width, depth (length), height.

CircularChamber  Centred on origin. Anchors: _entry (south), _exit (north),
                 _center, _far_end, _north/south/east/west, _perimeter_00…07.
                 Required dims: diameter, height.

RectangularRoom  Origin at south face. Anchors: _entry, _exit, _center,
                 _corner_ne/nw/se/sw, _wall_*_mid ×4.
                 Required dims: width, depth, height.

CrawlTunnel      Anchors: _entry, _mid, _exit.
                 Required dims: width, depth, height.

OpenArea         Anchors: _center, _edge_north/south/east/west, _edge_ne/nw/se/sw.
                 Required dims: radius (circular) OR width + depth (box).

Custom           No auto-generated anchors. Add with create_reference_point.

── DIMENSIONS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Pass only the fields relevant to the chosen zone_type. Omitted fields use
sensible defaults for that type.

{
  "width":        3.0,   "depth":       30.0,   "height":      3.0,
  "diameter":    20.0,   "step_count":  25,     "riser_height": 0.2,
  "turns":        2.5,   "radius":      10.0
}

── PARAMETERS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

zone_name:      GameObject name, e.g. "Zone1_Descent"
zone_type:      See zone type list above
dimensions:     Dict — only include fields relevant to this zone type
entry_position: World-space [x, y, z] of the zone entry. Default [0, 0, 0]
entry_rotation: Euler angles [x, y, z]. Default [0, 0, 0]
parent_path:    Scene hierarchy path of a container, e.g. "/ForgottenTunnels"
design_note:    Verbatim text from the design document for this zone
dressing_tags:  Ambient fill tags for bake step, e.g. ["dungeon", "damp"]

Returns: { zone_path, zone_type, anchors_created, anchor_paths[] }

tools.name: create_gameplay_marker
tools.summary: Places a GameplayMarker at a position in a ScaffoldZone.
tools.description:
Places a GameplayMarker at a position in a ScaffoldZone.

A GameplayMarker records functional intent WITHOUT referencing any specific
prefab. The prefab connection is made during the bake step via semantic_tags
matched against PrefabMetadata.tags[].

── MARKER TYPES ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

EnemySpawn     Enemy that spawns at this position
Trap           Trap or hazard
LootContainer  Container with items
Interaction    Interactable object (lever, valve, door, dialogue trigger)
AmbientDressing Environmental dressing hint for zone-level bake fill
Custom         Any other functional intent

── PLACEMENT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Provide anchor_path OR world_position. position_offset is added to either.
The marker is placed as a child of the zone containing anchor_path.
Use get_scaffold_anchors to list valid anchor paths.

── SEMANTIC TAGS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Matched against PrefabMetadata.tags[] during the bake resolve step.
Be specific — more overlap = better prefab match score:
  Bad:  ["enemy"]
  Good: ["enemy", "drowner", "undead", "sound_sensitive", "blind"]

── CONFIG ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Optional dict with marker-type-specific data. Stored as ConfigJson.

EnemySpawn:
  { "enemy_type": "AncientDrowner", "health": 80, "damage": 15,
    "detection_type": "hearing", "behavior": "stationary_head_tracking" }

Trap:
  { "trap_type": "squeaky_step", "alert_radius": 20.0,
    "trigger_condition": "walk", "crouch_reduction": 0.8,
    "fixable": true, "fix_item": "Oil",
    "fix_state_key": "squeaky_step_05_oiled" }

LootContainer:
  { "container_type": "skeleton",
    "loot_items": ["DryTeeth_x15", "OldKey", "DrownnerEssence"] }

── PARAMETERS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

detection_radius: World-space radius of the trigger/detection sphere.
                  Drawn as a translucent sphere in the scene view. 0 = none.

Returns: { marker_path, marker_type, position }

tools.name: resolve_scaffold_markers
tools.summary:
Matches each Pending GameplayMarker's semantic_tags against every
PrefabMetadata asset in the project and returns ranked prefab candidates.
tools.description:
Matches each Pending GameplayMarker's semantic_tags against every
PrefabMetadata asset in the project and returns ranked prefab candidates.

Call this after the scaffold is complete and before execute_bake.
Present the proposals to the user and wait for confirmation before baking.

── SCORING ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Each prefab is scored per marker:
  tag_overlap_count   — how many of the marker's semantic_tags appear
                        in the prefab's PrefabMetadata.tags[]
  scene_context_bonus — +1 per tag that also appears in the active
                        SceneContext.activeTags (set in McpBridgeSettings)
  total_score         — overlap + bonus, used for ranking

Candidates are returned sorted descending by total_score.
Ties are broken alphabetically by asset_path for stable ordering.

── RESPONSE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{
  "proposals": [
    {
      "marker_path":   "/ForgottenTunnels/Zone1_Descent/AncientDrowner_Mid",
      "marker_label":  "AncientDrowner_Mid",
      "marker_type":   "EnemySpawn",
      "semantic_tags": ["enemy", "drowner", "undead"],
      "candidates": [
        {
          "asset_guid":          "abc123...",
          "asset_path":          "Assets/Prefabs/Enemies/AncientDrowner.prefab",
          "display_name":        "Ancient Drowner",
          "tag_overlap_count":   3,
          "scene_context_bonus": 1,
          "total_score":         4
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "unresolvable": [
    {
      "marker_path":   "...",
      "marker_label":  "SqueakyStep_05",
      "semantic_tags": ["trap", "squeaky_step"]
    }
  ]
}

Markers in unresolvable had zero tag matches. Either add PrefabMetadata
to a suitable prefab, adjust the marker's semantic_tags, or skip those
markers and handle them manually.

── PARAMETERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

zone_path:                 Optional — restrict to one zone's markers.
                           Full hierarchy path, e.g. "/ForgottenTunnels/Zone1_Descent".
                           If omitted, all Pending markers in the scene are resolved.
marker_types:              Optional — filter by type, e.g. ["EnemySpawn", "LootContainer"].
                           If omitted, all types are included.
max_candidates_per_marker: How many ranked candidates to return per marker. Default 3.

tools.name: execute_bake
tools.summary:
Instantiates prefabs at confirmed GameplayMarker positions and marks each
marker as Baked. All operations are registered with Unity's Undo system.
tools.description:
Instantiates prefabs at confirmed GameplayMarker positions and marks each
marker as Baked. All operations are registered with Unity's Undo system.

Call this AFTER resolve_scaffold_markers and after the user has confirmed
(or you have selected) which prefab candidate to use for each marker.

── CONFIRMATIONS FORMAT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

confirmations = [
  {
    "marker_path": "/ForgottenTunnels/Zone1_Descent/AncientDrowner_Mid",
    "asset_guid":  "abc123..."
  },
  {
    "marker_path": "/ForgottenTunnels/Zone1_Descent/Loot_Skeleton_Bottom",
    "asset_guid":  "def456..."
  }
]

marker_path  — exact path from get_scaffold_markers or resolve_scaffold_markers
asset_guid   — the chosen candidate's asset_guid from resolve_scaffold_markers

── WHAT HAPPENS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

For each confirmation:
  1. The prefab is instantiated at the marker's world position and rotation
  2. The instance is named {marker_label}_Instance
  3. The instance is parented to the same zone container as the marker
  4. The marker's bake_state is set to Baked
  5. The marker's resolved_prefab_guid is set

Markers are NOT deleted — they stay in the scene as Baked (teal gizmo)
to record the design intent. Use hide_scaffold() to suppress them visually.

── PARAMETERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

confirmations:       List of { marker_path, asset_guid } pairs
hide_scaffold_after: If true, set the affected zone(s) inactive after baking.
                     Reversible via show_scaffold(). Default false.

Returns: { baked_count, instances[{ marker_label, instance_path }], warnings[] }

tools.name: get_cutscene_templates
tools.summary: Lists all available cutscene templates with their parameter schemas.
tools.description:
Lists all available cutscene templates with their parameter schemas.

Call this before create_cutscene_sequence to discover what templates are
available and what parameters each one requires.

Returns:
  cinemachine_version  — installed Cinemachine package version, or null if absent
  timeline_version     — installed Timeline package version
  templates[]          — list of templates, each with:
    name               — pass this as the 'template' argument to create_cutscene_sequence
    description        — what the template creates and when to use it
    parameters[]       — each parameter with name, type, required, default, description

If Cinemachine is not installed, templates is empty and message explains why.

Phase 1 available templates:
  DialogueCamera — over-shoulder / two-shot for NPC dialogue

tools.name: create_cutscene_sequence
tools.summary: Creates a cutscene sequence from a named template.
tools.description:
Creates a cutscene sequence from a named template.

Instantiates the template to produce:
  - A container GameObject under /Cutscenes/{sequence_name}/ in the scene
  - One or more Cinemachine virtual camera GameObjects
  - A Timeline .playable asset with Cinemachine, Activation, and Signal tracks
  - Signal assets in Assets/Cutscenes/Signals/ (reused across sequences)

── TEMPLATE: DialogueCamera ─────────────────────────────────────────────

Creates an over-shoulder / two-shot dialogue camera. Blends from the active
follow camera, holds during dialogue, then blends back.

Required params:
  player_path (string)  — hierarchy path of the player root, e.g. "/Player"
  npc_path    (string)  — hierarchy path of the NPC, e.g. "/Village/Merchant_A"
  duration    (float)   — total sequence length in seconds, e.g. 8.0

Optional params:
  camera_side (string)  — "left" | "right" | "front" | "auto" (default "auto")
                          "auto" places the camera on the side facing the current
                          Scene view camera at creation time.
  blend_in    (float)   — seconds to blend in from follow cam (default 0.5)
  blend_out   (float)   — seconds to blend back to follow cam (default 0.5)
  look_offset (float[3])— local offset from NPC root to look at (default [0,1.6,0])

Example:
  template      = "DialogueCamera"
  sequence_name = "DialogueCamera_MerchantA"
  params        = {
    "player_path": "/Player",
    "npc_path":    "/Village/Merchant_A",
    "camera_side": "right",
    "duration":    8.0,
    "blend_in":    0.5,
    "blend_out":   0.5,
    "look_offset": [0, 1.7, 0]
  }

── AFTER CREATION ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The sequence is created but not connected to any gameplay trigger.
The designer must:

1. Connect to a trigger (ALWAYS required):
     GetComponent<PlayableDirector>().Play();
   Wire this to an AnimationEvent, UnityEvent, proximity trigger, etc.

2. CinemachineBrain (if cinemachine_brain_found is false):
     Add a CinemachineBrain component to the Main Camera.

3. Signal receivers (when using dialogue_start / dialogue_end signals):
     Add a SignalReceiver to the player or dialogue manager.
     Wire dialogue_start → open dialogue UI
     Wire dialogue_end   → close dialogue UI, return control

── PARAMETERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

template:      Template name from get_cutscene_templates (e.g. "DialogueCamera")
sequence_name: Name for the scene container, e.g. "DialogueCamera_MerchantA"
params:        Template-specific parameter dict (see each template above)
timeline_path: Optional asset path for the .playable file.
               Defaults to "Assets/Cutscenes/{sequence_name}.playable"

Returns:
  { sequence_name, container_path, timeline_path, vcam_paths[],
    signals_created[], cinemachine_brain_found, warnings[] }

tools.name: preview_cutscene_sequence
tools.summary: Plays back an existing cutscene sequence in the Unity Editor.
tools.description:
Plays back an existing cutscene sequence in the Unity Editor.

Selects the container in the Hierarchy, opens the Timeline window,
resets playback to t=0, and calls PlayableDirector.Play().

container_path: full hierarchy path of the sequence container,
                e.g. "/Cutscenes/DialogueCamera_MerchantA"
                Use get_scene_hierarchy to find the path if unsure.

Useful for:
  - Checking that a newly created sequence looks right before committing
  - Reviewing a sequence after update_cutscene_sequence changes
  - Confirming signal timing and camera blend feel

Returns: { container_path, duration, message }

NOTE: Playback runs in the Editor scene view. The designer can stop it
at any time by clicking the Stop button in the Timeline window.
Calling preview_cutscene_sequence again resets to t=0 and replays.

tools.name: update_cutscene_sequence
tools.summary: Modifies an existing cutscene sequence in place.
tools.description:
Modifies an existing cutscene sequence in place.

Updates only the fields you provide — everything else is unchanged.
All changes are registered with Unity's Undo system.

── WHAT CAN BE UPDATED ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

ALL templates:
  duration    (float)   — total sequence length in seconds
  blend_in    (float)   — seconds to blend in (DialogueCamera, FocusCut)
  blend_out   (float)   — seconds to blend out (DialogueCamera, FocusCut)
  ease_in     (float)   — fraction for ease-in  (AreaReveal, ArrivalFlythrough)
  ease_out    (float)   — fraction for ease-out (AreaReveal, ArrivalFlythrough)

When duration or ease values change, the Timeline clip lengths, ActivationTrack
clip, signal marker positions, and cart animation curve are all updated together.

AreaReveal:
  waypoints   (float[3][])  — new camera path positions (min 2)
                              Updates CinemachineSmoothPath (CM2) or
                              SplineContainer knots (CM3) and rebakes the
                              cart animation curve.

ArrivalFlythrough:
  waypoints          (float[3][])  — new camera path (min 3)
  look_at_position   (float[3])    — new fixed world-space look target

FocusCut:
  camera_offset  (float[3])  — new offset from the target object to the camera,
                               e.g. [0, 1.5, -2.0]

DialogueCamera:
  look_offset  (float[3])  — adjusts the LookTarget height/position.
                             Y component is treated as absolute world height.

── EXAMPLE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Extend an AreaReveal and push the path further out
update_cutscene_sequence(
    container_path = "/Cutscenes/AreaReveal_DungeonEntrance",
    template       = "AreaReveal",
    params         = {
        "waypoints": [[0,10,0], [15,6,-15], [30,4,-28]],
        "duration":  9.0,
        "ease_out":  0.3
    }
)

# Tighten a FocusCut blend
update_cutscene_sequence(
    container_path = "/Cutscenes/FocusCut_AncientKey",
    template       = "FocusCut",
    params         = {
        "blend_in":  0.2,
        "blend_out": 0.3,
        "duration":  2.0
    }
)

── PARAMETERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

container_path: full hierarchy path returned by create_cutscene_sequence
template:       the template name used at creation (e.g. "AreaReveal")
params:         dict containing only the fields you want to change

Returns: { container_path, updated_fields[], warnings[] }

tools.name: find_objects
tools.summary: Searches the active scene for GameObjects matching one or more filters.
tools.description:
Searches the active scene for GameObjects matching one or more filters.

At least one filter must be provided. Filters are AND-combined.
Call get_scene_hierarchy instead if you need the full object tree.

── FILTERS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

tag             Exact Unity tag, e.g. "Interactable", "Enemy", "Prop"

component_type  Component type name from get_component_catalog,
                e.g. "Light", "Rigidbody", "NavMeshAgent", "AudioSource",
                or your own script names like "DialogueTrigger"

name_pattern    Glob pattern for the object name.
                * = any characters, ? = one character
                e.g. "Barrel*", "*Torch*", "Fence_??"
                Case-insensitive.

layer           Unity layer name, e.g. "Environment", "Pickable", "Default"

near_position   [x, y, z] world-space centre of a sphere query.
                Returns objects whose transform position is within
                near_radius metres (default 20m) of this point.
                Also catches collider-bearing objects via Physics.OverlapSphere.

── RESPONSE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Each object in the results array contains:
  name, path, position, rotation, scale, tag, layer, is_active, components[]

path is what other tools expect as object_path, e.g.:
  "/Village/Props/Barrel_04"
  "/World/Lighting/Lamp_03"

components[] lists the C# type names of every component on the object.

── EXAMPLES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# All lights within 30m of a point
find_objects(component_type="Light", near_position=[45, 0, 22], near_radius=30)

# All objects tagged "Prop" near a market stall
find_objects(tag="Prop", near_position=[45, 0, 22], near_radius=10)

# All objects whose name starts with "Barrel"
find_objects(name_pattern="Barrel*")

# All NavMesh obstacles in the scene
find_objects(component_type="NavMeshObstacle")

# All objects on the Environment layer near a camp
find_objects(layer="Environment", near_position=[100, 0, 50], near_radius=25)

include_inactive: include inactive GameObjects (default false)
max_results:      cap on returned objects (default 100)

tools.name: get_object_properties
tools.summary: Reads the serialised property values of a component on a scene object.
tools.description:
Reads the serialised property values of a component on a scene object.

WORKFLOW: call get_component_catalog to find property_path strings,
then call this to read current values, then set_object_properties to change them.

object_path:    hierarchy path from get_scene_hierarchy or find_objects,
                e.g. "/Village/Lamp_03"

component_type: type_name from get_component_catalog, e.g. "Light", "Rigidbody"

property_paths: list of specific property paths to read, e.g.
                ["m_Intensity", "m_Color", "m_Range"]
                If omitted, returns all top-level serialised properties.
                Use get_component_catalog to find valid property paths.

RESPONSE per property:
  property_path  — exact path to use in set_object_properties
  value          — current value (float, int, bool, string, [r,g,b,a], etc.)
  type           — Float | Integer | Boolean | String | Color | Vector3 |
                   Enum:LightType[Spot|Directional|Point|Area] | ObjectReference | ...

EXAMPLE — read a light's current settings:
  get_object_properties("/Village/Lamp_03", "Light",
                        ["m_Intensity", "m_Color", "m_Range", "m_Type"])

tools.name: set_object_properties
tools.summary:
Modifies serialised property values on a component that already exists
on a scene object. All changes are registered with Unity's Undo system.
tools.description:
Modifies serialised property values on a component that already exists
on a scene object. All changes are registered with Unity's Undo system.

object_path:    hierarchy path of the target object
component_type: type_name from get_component_catalog
create_if_missing: if true, adds the component if it isn't present
                   (same as add_component_to_object). Default false.

PROPERTIES FORMAT:
  List of { "property_path": "...", "value": ... } — identical format to
  add_component_to_object. Use property_path values from get_component_catalog
  or from get_object_properties.

  float/int   → number:           1.5
  bool        → boolean:          true
  string      → string:           "name"
  enum        → string:           "Point"  (use enum_names from catalog)
  Vector3     → array:            [0, -9.81, 0]
  Color       → array [r,g,b,a]:  [1.0, 0.85, 0.6, 1.0]
  ObjectRef   → object:           { "asset_guid": "abc123..." }

EXAMPLE — normalise a light that's too bright:
  set_object_properties(
      "/Village/Lamp_03",
      "Light",
      [
        { "property_path": "m_Intensity", "value": 1.0 },
        { "property_path": "m_Color",     "value": [1.0, 0.85, 0.6, 1.0] }
      ]
  )

Returns: { object_path, component_type, applied_properties[], failed_properties[], warnings[] }

tools.name: set_object_metadata
tools.summary:
Sets identity properties on one or more GameObjects in a single Undo-able call.
Accepts a list of paths so an entire dressing pass can be tagged/layered/flagged
at once without iterating each object individually.
tools.description:
Sets identity properties on one or more GameObjects in a single Undo-able call.
Accepts a list of paths so an entire dressing pass can be tagged/layered/flagged
at once without iterating each object individually.

Only the fields you provide are updated. Omitted fields are unchanged.

object_paths:  one or more hierarchy paths (bulk)

name:          rename the object(s). For a single object: exact name.
               For multiple objects: "Barrel" → Barrel_01, Barrel_02, ...

tag:           Unity tag name. Must already exist in Project Settings → Tags.
               e.g. "Prop", "Interactable", "Enemy", "Environment"

layer:         Unity layer name, e.g. "Default", "Environment", "Pickable"

static_flags:  list of one or more:
                 "LightmapStatic"        (also accepts "ContributeGI" for Unity 2022+)
                 "OccluderStatic"
                 "BatchingStatic"
                 "NavigationStatic"
                 "OccludeeStatic"
                 "ReflectionProbeStatic"
                 "OffMeshLinkGeneration"
               Pass ["All"] to set every flag. Pass ["None"] to clear all.

is_active:     set the GameObject active or inactive

EXAMPLE — mark 30 placed props for lightmap baking:
  set_object_metadata(
      object_paths=[...30 paths from dress_area...],
      tag="Prop",
      layer="Environment",
      static_flags=["LightmapStatic", "OccluderStatic"]
  )

Returns: { updated_count, applied[], warnings[] }

tools.name: reparent_objects
tools.summary:
Moves one or more objects to a new parent in the hierarchy.
Registered with Unity's Undo system.
tools.description:
Moves one or more objects to a new parent in the hierarchy.
Registered with Unity's Undo system.

object_paths:        objects to move
new_parent_path:     hierarchy path of the new parent.
                     Pass null or omit to move objects to the scene root.
keep_world_position: if true, the object stays at its current world-space
                     position after reparenting (default true).
                     If false, the local transform is preserved instead.

EXAMPLE — organise placed objects into a container:
  reparent_objects(
      object_paths=["/Barrel_01", "/Barrel_02", "/Crate_03"],
      new_parent_path="/Village/MarketStall_NE"
  )

Returns: { reparented_count, warnings[] }

tools.name: duplicate_objects
tools.summary:
Creates one or more copies of existing scene objects, preserving all
components and property values. All copies are registered with Undo.
tools.description:
Creates one or more copies of existing scene objects, preserving all
components and property values. All copies are registered with Undo.

object_paths:    objects to duplicate (each gets `count` copies)

count:           number of copies per source object (default 1)

position_offset: world-space offset applied CUMULATIVELY per copy.
                 e.g. [4, 0, 0] with count=5 places copies at +4m, +8m,
                 +12m, +16m, +20m from the source. Default [0, 0, 0].

rotation_offset: Euler angle offset applied cumulatively per copy.
                 e.g. [0, 45, 0] with count=4 gives 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°
                 Y-rotation offset. Default [0, 0, 0].

parent_path:     parent for all duplicates. Uses each source's own parent
                 if omitted.

name_suffix:     string appended to the source name for each copy, e.g.
                 "_Mirror" → SourceName_Mirror.
                 If omitted: _Copy, _Copy_2, _Copy_3, ...

EXAMPLES:
  # Line up 5 lamp posts at 4m intervals along Z
  duplicate_objects(
      object_paths=["/Village/LampPost_A"],
      count=5,
      position_offset=[0, 0, 4]
  )

  # Make 3 copies of a stall in a square
  duplicate_objects(
      object_paths=["/Village/MarketStall_Template"],
      count=3,
      position_offset=[6, 0, 0],
      parent_path="/Village/Stalls"
  )

Returns: { created_count, paths[], warnings[] }

tools.name: snap_to_surface
tools.summary: Raycasts from each object's position and moves it to the hit surface.
tools.description:
Raycasts from each object's position and moves it to the hit surface.

This fixes the most common dressing error: objects floating above the
ground or sinking into a slope after placement.

object_paths:    objects to snap (accepts one or many)

cast_direction:  [x, y, z] direction vector for the raycast.
                 Default [0, -1, 0] (straight down onto the terrain/floor).
                 Use [0, 1, 0] to snap to a ceiling, or a custom direction
                 for wall snapping.

max_distance:    how far to cast in metres (default 100)

surface_offset:  gap to leave above the hit surface in metres (default 0).
                 Use a small positive value (e.g. 0.01) if objects are
                 sinking into the surface due to pivot placement.

align_to_normal: rotate the object so its up-axis matches the surface
                 normal (default false). Useful for rocks and organic props
                 on slopes. Keep false for furniture and buildings.

layer_mask:      Unity layer bitmask to restrict which surfaces are hit.
                 Null = all layers (default). Use e.g. 1 << 8 to hit only
                 the Terrain layer.

EXAMPLES:
  # Snap a row of barrels to the ground after placement
  snap_to_surface(["/Village/Barrel_01", "/Village/Barrel_02"])

  # Snap rocks to a slope and tilt them to match the normal
  snap_to_surface(rock_paths, align_to_normal=True)

  # Snap props with a 2cm clearance (pivot is at centre, not base)
  snap_to_surface(paths, surface_offset=0.02)

Returns: { snapped_count, skipped: [{ path, reason }] }

tools.name: align_and_distribute
tools.summary: Repositions a set of objects relative to each other using one of four modes.
tools.description:
Repositions a set of objects relative to each other using one of four modes.

── MODES ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

distribute_between
  Evenly spaces N objects in a straight line between two world-space
  points. If face_direction=True (default), each object is rotated to
  face along the line.

  Required: start_point=[x,y,z], end_point=[x,y,z]
  Optional: face_direction (default true)

  EXAMPLE — 6 fence posts between two corners:
    align_and_distribute(
        fence_post_paths, "distribute_between",
        start_point=[10,0,0], end_point=[10,0,20],
        face_direction=True
    )

align_to_axis
  Shifts all objects so a specified edge of their bounding box aligns
  to a given axis value. Use this to level a row of crates to the
  same Y height, or flush a line of objects against a wall.

  Required: axis ("x"|"y"|"z"), value (float)
  Optional: use_pivot ("min"|"center"|"max", default "center")

  EXAMPLE — level all object bottoms to Y=0:
    align_and_distribute(
        crate_paths, "align_to_axis",
        axis="y", value=0.0, use_pivot="min"
    )

stack
  Stacks objects on top of each other along the stack_axis, using each
  object's bounds to determine height so the stack doesn't float or clip.

  Optional: stack_axis ("x"|"y"|"z", default "y"),
            base_position [x,y,z] (default: first object's current position)

  EXAMPLE — stack three crates:
    align_and_distribute(
        [crate_bottom, crate_mid, crate_top], "stack",
        stack_axis="y", base_position=[5, 0, 5]
    )

circle
  Evenly distributes objects around a horizontal circle. If
  facing_outward=True (default), each object faces away from the centre.

  Required: center=[x,y,z], radius (float)
  Optional: facing_outward (default true), start_angle_degrees (default 0)

  EXAMPLE — 8 torches around a ritual circle:
    align_and_distribute(
        torch_paths, "circle",
        center=[0, 0, 0], radius=5.0,
        facing_outward=False
    )

── RETURNS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{ repositioned_count, warnings[] }

tools.name: randomize_transforms
tools.summary:
Applies bounded random offsets to position, rotation, and/or scale on a
set of objects.
tools.description:
Applies bounded random offsets to position, rotation, and/or scale on a
set of objects.

This is the difference between dressing that looks placed by a computer
and dressing that looks like it was actually used. A row of identical barrels
with ±15° Y rotation and ±10% scale variation reads as lived-in; without it,
it reads as a prefab row.

object_paths:   objects to vary (at least one of the range params required)

seed:           integer seed for the random generator. If omitted, a random
                seed is chosen and returned in the response so you can
                reproduce or describe the result later.

position_range: [x, y, z] max offset per axis (applied symmetrically ±).
                e.g. [0.3, 0, 0.3] shuffles XZ by up to ±30cm, no Y change.

rotation_range: [x, y, z] max rotation offset in degrees per axis.
                e.g. [0, 180, 0]  — full random Y (good for crates, rocks)
                e.g. [5, 180, 5]  — slight XZ tilt plus full Y (good for rocks)
                e.g. [0, 15, 0]   — subtle ±15° Y (good for furniture)

scale_range:    [min, max] uniform scale multiplier applied to each object
                independently. e.g. [0.85, 1.15] gives ±15% size variation.
                Applied as a multiplier on top of the current local scale.

snap_after:     if True, each object is raycasted downward and snapped to
                the surface below after randomization. Useful after adding
                position_range that shifts objects off the ground.

EXAMPLES:
  # Natural variation for a row of barrels
  randomize_transforms(
      barrel_paths,
      rotation_range=[0, 180, 0],
      scale_range=[0.9, 1.1]
  )

  # Rock scatter with tilt, full rotation, and size variation
  randomize_transforms(
      rock_paths,
      rotation_range=[15, 180, 15],
      scale_range=[0.6, 1.4],
      snap_after=True
  )

  # Subtle shuffle for market stall props (preserves ground contact)
  randomize_transforms(
      stall_paths,
      position_range=[0.2, 0, 0.2],
      rotation_range=[0, 20, 0],
      snap_after=True
  )

Returns: { randomized_count, seed_used, warnings[] }
seed_used is the seed that was actually applied — record it if you want
to reproduce this exact variation later.

tools.name: group_objects
tools.summary:
Creates a new empty GameObject, positions it at the group pivot, and
reparents all specified objects under it. The programmatic equivalent of
selecting a set of objects and pressing Ctrl+G in the hierarchy.
tools.description:
Creates a new empty GameObject, positions it at the group pivot, and
reparents all specified objects under it. The programmatic equivalent of
selecting a set of objects and pressing Ctrl+G in the hierarchy.

After a dress_area pass or a scatter run, calling group_objects keeps the
hierarchy navigable and makes the entire dressed location easy to select,
move, or disable as a unit.

object_paths: objects to group

group_name:   name for the new container, e.g. "MarketStall_NE_Clutter",
              "RitualCircle_Torches", "BanditCamp_Tent_A"

parent_path:  where to create the container in the hierarchy.
              If omitted, uses the common ancestor of the grouped objects
              (or the scene root if they have none).

pivot:        where to place the container's origin:
              "center"       — centroid of all grouped objects (default)
              "first"        — position of the first object in the list
              "world_origin" — (0, 0, 0)

tag:          optional tag for the container object

layer:        optional layer for the container object

EXAMPLES:
  # Organise the output of a dress_area call
  group_objects(
      object_paths=placed_paths,
      group_name="MarketStall_NE",
      parent_path="/Village/Dressing"
  )

  # Group ritual torches with a shared tag
  group_objects(
      torch_paths,
      group_name="RitualCircle",
      pivot="center",
      tag="RitualProp"
  )

Returns: { container_path, grouped_count, warnings[] }
container_path is the hierarchy path of the newly created container — use
it in subsequent reparent_objects or set_object_metadata calls.

tools.name: create_trigger_volume
tools.summary:
Creates a complete trigger GameObject in one call: a named empty object
with an isTrigger collider, optional tag, optional layer, and an optional
MonoBehaviour script with pre-configured properties.
tools.description:
Creates a complete trigger GameObject in one call: a named empty object
with an isTrigger collider, optional tag, optional layer, and an optional
MonoBehaviour script with pre-configured properties.

Open-world games use hundreds of trigger volumes — dialogue triggers, zone
transitions, combat arenas, loot proximity detectors, ambient sound regions.
Currently setting one up requires ~5 separate tool calls. This does it in one.

name:     GameObject name, e.g. "DialogueTrigger_Elder", "SpawnZone_BanditCamp"

position: [x, y, z] world-space centre of the trigger volume

shape:    "box"     — BoxCollider (default)
          "sphere"  — SphereCollider
          "capsule" — CapsuleCollider

── SIZE PARAMETERS (pick the right ones for your shape) ─────────────────

For box:
  size=[width, height, depth]   e.g. size=[3.0, 2.5, 3.0]

For sphere:
  radius=1.5                    OR  size=[1.5]

For capsule:
  radius=0.5, height=2.0       OR  size=[0.5, 2.0]

If size/radius/height are all omitted, sensible defaults are used
(1×1×1 box, 0.5m sphere radius, 0.5r×2h capsule).

── IDENTITY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

tag:    Unity tag name. Must already exist in Project Settings → Tags.
        e.g. "DialogueTrigger", "CombatZone", "QuestTrigger"

layer:  Unity layer name, e.g. "Triggers", "Default"

── SCRIPT COMPONENT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

script_component:   type_name of a MonoBehaviour to add, from
                    get_component_catalog. e.g. "DialogueTrigger",
                    "QuestTrigger", "SpawnZone"

script_properties:  list of { "property_path": "...", "value": ... }
                    to set on the added script. Same format as
                    add_component_to_object.
                    Supported types: float, int, bool, string, enum.
                    For Vector3/Color/ObjectReference use set_object_properties
                    on the returned object_path afterward.

EXAMPLES:
  # Simple dialogue trigger box
  create_trigger_volume(
      name="DialogueTrigger_Elder",
      shape="box",
      position=[45.0, 1.0, 22.0],
      size=[3.0, 2.5, 3.0],
      tag="DialogueTrigger",
      layer="Triggers",
      script_component="DialogueTrigger",
      script_properties=[
          {"property_path": "dialogueId",   "value": "elder_intro"},
          {"property_path": "triggerOnce",  "value": True}
      ],
      parent_path="/World/Triggers"
  )

  # Sphere-shaped spawn zone, no script
  create_trigger_volume(
      name="SpawnZone_Bandits",
      shape="sphere",
      position=[100.0, 0.0, 50.0],
      radius=8.0,
      tag="SpawnZone",
      layer="Triggers"
  )

Returns: {
  object_path,      ← use this in set_object_properties for complex script fields
  shape,
  effective_size,   ← [w,h,d] for box, [r] for sphere, [r,h] for capsule
  tag,
  script_added,     ← null if no script, component name if added
  warnings[]
}

tools.name: apply_material
tools.summary: Assigns a material to the MeshRenderer of one or more scene objects.
tools.description:
Assigns a material to the MeshRenderer of one or more scene objects.

Exactly one of material_name, material_path, or material_tag must be
provided. For visual variety across a set of identical props, use
material_tag + random_from_tag=True.

object_paths:   objects to modify (must have MeshRenderer components)

── MATERIAL LOOKUP (use exactly one) ────────────────────────────────────

material_name:  exact asset name in the project, e.g. "Wood_Dark_Worn".
                Matches by name == comparison (case-sensitive).

material_path:  full asset database path,
                e.g. "Assets/Materials/Props/Wood_Dark_Worn.mat"
                Use this when multiple materials share the same name.

material_tag:   case-insensitive name-contains search across all project
                materials. e.g. "wood" finds Wood_Dark, Wood_Pale_Old,
                BrokenWood_Planks, etc.
                Combined with random_from_tag=True this assigns a different
                material from the matching pool to each object.

── OPTIONS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

random_from_tag:  when True and multiple materials match material_tag,
                  each object gets a independently-chosen material from
                  the pool rather than all getting the same one.
                  Ignored when using material_name or material_path
                  (single candidate by definition). Default false.

material_slot:    which MeshRenderer material index to replace.
                  Default 0 (the primary material). Use 1, 2, etc. for
                  multi-material meshes (e.g. a building with separate
                  wall and roof materials).

EXAMPLES:
  # Same material on all crates
  apply_material(
      object_paths=crate_paths,
      material_name="Wood_Dark_Worn"
  )

  # Different wood variant on each barrel (visual variety)
  apply_material(
      object_paths=barrel_paths,
      material_tag="wood",
      random_from_tag=True
  )

  # Replace only the roof material (slot 1) on a building
  apply_material(
      object_paths=["/Village/Barn"],
      material_name="Thatch_Old",
      material_slot=1
  )

Returns: {
  applied_count,
  assignments: [{ path, material }],   ← which material went on which object
  warnings[]
}

tools.name: dress_area
tools.summary:
Fill a circular area with prefabs chosen to match a plain-language intent
(e.g. "medieval market stall with crates and barrels"), submitted as a
proposal for review: nothing is placed until execute_proposal.
tools.description:
Fill a circular area with prefabs chosen to match a plain-language intent
(e.g. "medieval market stall with crates and barrels"), submitted as a
proposal for review: nothing is placed until execute_proposal.

Given a world-space centre, a radius, and a natural-language description
of what you want in the area, dress_area:
  1. Scores every prefab in the catalog against your intent
  2. Generates well-distributed candidate positions (Poisson disk)
  3. Discards positions that overlap existing scene objects
  4. Raycasts each surviving position to the nearest surface below
  5. Assigns a prefab to each position (weighted by relevance)
  6. Submits everything as a proposal to the Operation Queue for review

Nothing is placed until you call execute_proposal with the returned
proposal_id. The Operation Queue window shows every proposed item with
its position and prefab name; you can approve, reject, or edit individual
items before executing.

── PARAMETERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

center:   [x, y, z] world-space centre of the area to fill

radius:   radius of the circular area in metres

intent:   natural-language description of what you want.
          Words are matched against PrefabMetadata tags, categories,
          and display names — the more specific the better.

          Good intents:
            "neglected medieval market stall with crates and barrels"
            "dungeon corridor with wall sconces and debris on the floor"
            "forest clearing with fallen logs, mushrooms, and rocks"
            "bandit camp cooking area with firepit props and sacks"

          The scoring is tag-overlap based. If a prefab has tags
          ["crate", "wooden", "medieval"] and your intent contains
          "medieval crates", that prefab scores 2 and is much more
          likely to be selected than one with no matching tags.

density:  "sparse"  — ~5-15 objects, 2m min spacing
          "medium"  — ~10-25 objects, 1.2m min spacing (default)
          "dense"   — ~20-40 objects, 0.7m min spacing

exclude_tags:  prefab tags to never use, e.g. ["futuristic", "sci-fi"]

include_tags:  if provided, only prefabs matching at least one of these
               tags are considered. Useful for narrowing to a specific
               asset set without relying on intent scoring.

snap_to_surfaces:  raycast each candidate position downward and land it
                   on the terrain/floor (default True).

avoid_existing:    skip positions that overlap existing scene colliders
                   within avoidance_radius (default True).

avoidance_radius:  minimum clearance from existing objects in metres
                   (default 0.5m). Reduce to 0.1 for tight spaces.

parent_path:  if provided, each placed prefab gets this parent. Leave
              null and use group_objects afterward to organise the result.

group_name:   name used in the proposal summary, e.g. "MarketStall_NE".
              Defaults to a position-derived name.

── WORKFLOW ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. dress_area(...)             → returns proposal_id + summary
2. [Review Operation Queue]    → approve/reject individual items
3. execute_proposal(proposal_id)
4. snap_to_surface(placed_paths)    ← optional cleanup pass
5. randomize_transforms(placed_paths, rotation_range=[0,180,0])
6. set_object_metadata(placed_paths, tag="Prop", static_flags=["LightmapStatic"])
7. group_objects(placed_paths, group_name="MarketStall_NE_Clutter")

── EXAMPLES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Market stall clutter, 8m radius
dress_area(
    center=[45.0, 0.0, 22.0],
    radius=8.0,
    intent="busy medieval market stall crates barrels sacks hanging lantern",
    density="medium",
    include_tags=["medieval", "prop"],
    group_name="MarketStall_NE"
)

# Sparse dungeon entrance dressing
dress_area(
    center=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
    radius=12.0,
    intent="dungeon entrance rocks rubble bones skulls torches",
    density="sparse",
    exclude_tags=["village", "urban"]
)

# Dense forest floor coverage
dress_area(
    center=[100.0, 0.0, 50.0],
    radius=15.0,
    intent="forest floor ferns mushrooms fallen logs rocks",
    density="dense",
    snap_to_surfaces=True
)

── RETURNS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{
  "proposal_id":     "prop_a3f2b1c4",  ← pass to execute_proposal
  "summary":         "14 props proposed for ...",
  "proposed_count":  14,
  "discarded_count": 3,  ← positions too close to existing objects
  "group_name":      "MarketStall_NE",
  "warnings":        [...]
}

The summary breaks down the proposal by prefab type so you can see
at a glance what was selected before opening the Operation Queue.

tools.name: query_terrain
tools.summary:
Sample terrain height, surface normal, slope, and layer weights at one or more
world-space positions.
tools.description:
Sample terrain height, surface normal, slope, and layer weights at one or more
world-space positions.

CALL THIS BEFORE PLACING OBJECTS to validate that positions are suitable:
  - slope_degrees > 30–35 typically means too steep for buildings and fences
  - layer_weights shows what texture is painted there (grass, road, water, etc.)
  - surface_height gives the actual Y coordinate to snap objects to terrain level

Positions outside all active terrain tiles return error="NO_TERRAIN" with null
fields. The rest of the batch succeeds normally — partial terrain coverage is fine.

Parameters
----------
positions : list of [x, y, z]
    World-space positions to sample. The Y component is ignored for sampling
    but echoed back in the response. Pass all candidate positions in one call.
include_layer_weights : bool
    Whether to return per-layer alpha weights (default True). Set False when
    you only need height/normal to reduce overhead on high-resolution terrain.

Returns per-position
--------------------
surface_height : float  — Y in world space at that point
normal         : [x,y,z] — interpolated surface normal (unit vector)
slope_degrees  : float  — steepness in degrees (0 = flat, 90 = cliff)
terrain_name   : str    — name of the Terrain tile covering this position
layer_weights  : [{layer_name, weight}] — terrain layer alpha values (sum ≈ 1.0)
error          : str | null — "NO_TERRAIN" if no tile covers the position

tools.name: bake_navmesh
tools.summary: Build one or more NavMeshSurface components in the active scene.
tools.description:
Build one or more NavMeshSurface components in the active scene.

Requires the Unity AI Navigation package (com.unity.ai.navigation).
Returns PACKAGE_NOT_INSTALLED if the package is missing.

Call this at the end of any operation that adds, moves, or removes objects
with geometry that affects walkable surfaces — including dress_area,
scatter_prefabs, place_prefab, and set_navmesh_area.

Selection priority (first matching rule wins):
  1. surface_paths — bake the specific surfaces on those hierarchy paths
  2. agent_type_name — bake all surfaces for that agent type (e.g. "Humanoid")
  3. all=True — bake every NavMeshSurface in the active scene
  4. default — bake only the first surface found

For most open-world dressing workflows, all=True is the correct choice.
Use surface_paths or agent_type_name only when you know which tile(s) changed.

Parameters
----------
surface_paths   : list of hierarchy paths to NavMeshSurface GameObjects
all             : bake every surface in the scene (default False)
agent_type_name : only bake surfaces matching this agent type name

tools.name: set_navmesh_area
tools.summary:
Assign a NavMesh area type to objects (via NavMeshModifier component) or create
a floating volumetric override (via NavMeshModifierVolume).
tools.description:
Assign a NavMesh area type to objects (via NavMeshModifier component) or create
a floating volumetric override (via NavMeshModifierVolume).

Requires the Unity AI Navigation package (com.unity.ai.navigation).

area_name must match a name in Project Settings > Navigation (or Navigation > Areas
in the AI Navigation window). Common built-in names: "Walkable", "Not Walkable",
"Jump". Custom names (e.g. "Water", "Road") are defined per-project.

On unknown area_name, the response includes a 'warnings' list of all available
names — check that to correct the call.

Always call bake_navmesh after to apply the changes to the NavMesh data.

Parameters
----------
area_name     : NavMesh area name (case-sensitive, must match project settings)
object_paths  : hierarchy paths of existing objects to add NavMeshModifier to
override_area : whether the modifier overrides child hierarchy areas (default True)
volume        : dict to create a NavMeshModifierVolume instead of a component.
                Shape: {
                  "position": [x, y, z],   # world-space centre
                  "size":     [w, h, d],    # extents in world units
                  "rotation": [x, y, z],   # optional Euler angles
                  "name":     "...",        # optional GameObject name
                  "parent_path": "..."      # optional hierarchy parent
                }

Example — mark a water plane and block a courtyard:
    set_navmesh_area("Water",        object_paths=["/World/WaterPlane"])
    set_navmesh_area("Not Walkable", volume={"position":[0,1,0], "size":[20,4,20]})
    bake_navmesh(all=True)

tools.name: get_loaded_scenes
tools.summary: List all scenes currently loaded in the Unity Editor.
tools.description:
List all scenes currently loaded in the Unity Editor.

Returns name, asset path, active status, and dirty flag for each.
Use this before manage_scene to understand the current state:
  - is_active: True for the scene that receives new objects by default
  - is_dirty:  True if the scene has unsaved changes

In a streaming open-world setup, you typically have one or two terrain tile
scenes loaded additively alongside the base scene. This call shows you exactly
what is open before you load, unload, or move objects between scenes.

tools.name: manage_scene
tools.summary:
Multi-scene operations in the editor: list, load (additively), unload or
create scenes, and move objects from one loaded scene to another.
tools.description:
Multi-scene operations in the editor: list, load (additively), unload or
create scenes, and move objects from one loaded scene to another.

Operations
----------
"list"
    Same as get_loaded_scenes — returns all loaded scenes.
    No additional parameters required.

"load"
    Load a scene additively alongside the current ones.
    scene_path  : required, e.g. "Assets/Scenes/Village_NW.unity"
    set_active  : optional, make it the active scene (default False)

"unload"
    Remove an additively-loaded scene from the editor.
    scene_path  : required — asset path or scene name
    Fails if this is the only loaded scene.

"move_objects"
    Move one or more scene objects from their current scene into another.
    object_paths      : required — list of hierarchy paths to move
    target_scene_name : required — name of the destination scene (must be loaded)
    Objects with parents NOT in the move list are detached first (a warning is
    returned for each detachment).

"create"
    Create a new empty scene asset and load it additively.
    scene_path        : required, e.g. "Assets/Scenes/Village_SE.unity"
    set_active        : optional, make it the active scene (default False)
    save_after_create : optional, write the .unity file immediately (default True)

Common workflow — fix misplaced objects across a tile boundary:
    get_loaded_scenes()
    manage_scene("load", scene_path="Assets/Scenes/Village_NW.unity")
    find_objects(name_pattern="Barrel*", near_position=[...])
    manage_scene("move_objects",
                 object_paths=[...],
                 target_scene_name="Village_NE")
    manage_scene("unload", scene_path="Assets/Scenes/Village_NW.unity")

tools.name: validate_scene
tools.summary: Run diagnostic checks across the active scene and return a structured issue report.
tools.description:
Run diagnostic checks across the active scene and return a structured issue report.

Each check returns a list of object hierarchy paths with detail strings. The agent
can present this report conversationally and use other tools (set_object_metadata,
snap_to_surface, etc.) to fix the flagged issues.

Available check IDs
-------------------
"missing_scripts"
    error — GameObjects with missing MonoBehaviour script references.
    Common after a script rename, refactor, or package removal.

"missing_materials"
    error — MeshRenderers with one or more null material slots.
    Common after a material asset is deleted.

"untagged_triggers"
    warning — Trigger colliders whose GameObject has tag "Untagged".
    Almost always a forgotten configuration step.

"duplicate_names"
    warning — Siblings with identical names under the same parent.
    Breaks FindByPath and causes confusing hierarchy navigation.

"meshrenderer_no_collider"
    info — MeshRenderers with no Collider on the same object.
    Opt-in: generates false positives for decorative-only objects.

"large_light_range"
    info — Point/Spot lights with range > light_range_threshold.
    Catches accidentally large values left from tweaking sessions.

"floating_objects"
    info — Renderable objects with no surface detected within
    floating_ray_distance below their pivot. Catches props left
    floating after terrain was sculpted beneath them.
    Opt-in: generates false positives for intentionally elevated objects.

Parameters
----------
checks                : list of check IDs to run. None = run all checks.
scope_path            : hierarchy path to restrict the scan. None = full active scene.
max_results_per_check : cap on issues returned per check (default 50).
light_range_threshold : range in metres for the large_light_range check (default 100.0).
floating_ray_distance : downward ray distance in metres for floating_objects (default 0.5).

Returns
-------
{
  total_issues : int,
  checks_run   : [str],
  results      : [
    {
      check_id    : str,
      severity    : "error" | "warning" | "info",
      description : str,
      count       : int,
      issues      : [{ path: str, detail: str }]
    }
  ]
}

Workflow example
----------------
# End-of-session quality pass
validate_scene(checks=["missing_scripts", "missing_materials", "untagged_triggers"])
# → agent presents issues, then fixes tags with set_object_metadata and
#   snaps floating props with snap_to_surface

tools.name: create_audio_zone
tools.summary: Create an audio zone at a world-space position.
tools.description:
Create an audio zone at a world-space position.

zone_type="reverb_zone"
    Creates a GameObject with an AudioReverbZone component.
    Shapes the acoustic environment — adds echo, dampening, and spatial character
    to all audio sources within range. No AudioClip required.
    Use for caves, interiors, underwater, large outdoor spaces.

    preset is required. Available presets:
      "cave"        → Unity Cave reverb
      "forest"      → Forest (muffled, organic)
      "dungeon"     → Stone Corridor (stone, enclosed)
      "interior"    → Room (wooden/plaster interior)
      "exterior"    → Plain (open outdoor)
      "underwater"  → Underwater
      "cathedral"   → Concert Hall (large resonant space)
      "alley"       → Alley (narrow urban)

zone_type="ambient_source"
    Creates a fully-3D AudioSource with linear rolloff and a SphereCollider trigger
    (trigger-only, for scene-view visualisation — no physics effect).
    Use for streams, campfires, wind, distant machinery.

    audio_clip_path is recommended. If omitted, the source is created without a clip
    and a warning is returned — assign a clip manually in the Inspector.

Parameters
----------
zone_type       : "reverb_zone" or "ambient_source"
position        : [x, y, z] world-space centre
min_distance    : inner radius in metres — full effect / direct sound (default 1.0)
max_distance    : outer radius in metres — effect fades to zero (default 10.0)
preset          : reverb preset name (required for reverb_zone)
audio_clip_path : AssetDatabase path to AudioClip (for ambient_source)
volume          : 0.0–1.0 playback volume for ambient_source (default 1.0)
loop            : loop playback for ambient_source (default True)
play_on_awake   : auto-play on scene start for ambient_source (default True)
parent_path     : optional hierarchy parent path
name            : optional GameObject name

Biome transition example
------------------------
# Dungeon entrance — acoustic + ambient in two calls
create_audio_zone("reverb_zone", [0,2,0],
                  preset="dungeon", min_distance=3.0, max_distance=15.0)
create_audio_zone("ambient_source", [0,2,0],
                  audio_clip_path="Assets/Audio/Ambient/DungeonDrips.wav",
                  min_distance=2.0, max_distance=12.0, volume=0.6)

tools.name: create_postprocessing_volume
tools.summary:
Create a URP Volume GameObject with a VolumeProfile containing the specified
post-processing overrides.
tools.description:
Create a URP Volume GameObject with a VolumeProfile containing the specified
post-processing overrides.

Requires the Unity AI Navigation package — returns PACKAGE_NOT_INSTALLED if
com.unity.render-pipelines.universal is absent.

Effect names
------------
Use the exact C# class name from the UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal namespace.
Names are matched case-insensitively. Common ones:

  Bloom              — intensity, threshold, scatter, tint ([r,g,b,a])
  ColorAdjustments   — postExposure, contrast, colorFilter, hueShift, saturation
  DepthOfField       — mode ("Off"|"Gaussian"|"Bokeh"), focusDistance, aperture,
                       focalLength, gaussianStart, gaussianEnd
  FilmGrain          — type ("Thin1"|"Medium1"|...|"Custom"), intensity, response
  LensDistortion     — intensity, xMultiplier, yMultiplier, center ([x,y]), scale
  MotionBlur         — mode ("CameraVelocity"|"ObjectVelocity"), quality, intensity
  ShadowsMidtonesHighlights — shadows/midtones/highlights ([r,g,b,a])
  Tonemapping        — mode ("None"|"Neutral"|"ACES"|"Custom")
  Vignette           — color ([r,g,b,a]), center ([x,y]), intensity, smoothness
  WhiteBalance       — temperature, tint
  ChromaticAberration — intensity

Property types
--------------
float/int/bool   — pass as JSON number / boolean
enum             — pass as string (e.g. "ACES") or int index
Color            — pass as [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] array (0.0–1.0 range)
Vector2          — pass as [x, y] array
Vector4          — pass as [x, y, z, w] array

Parameters
----------
overrides      : list of {"effect": "EffectName", "properties": {"field": value}}
profile_name   : name for new profile asset saved to Assets/Volumes/ (default "PostProcessVolume")
profile_path   : AssetDatabase path to an existing VolumeProfile to reuse and modify
position       : [x, y, z] world-space centre (required for non-global volumes)
size           : [w, h, d] box extents for the volume bounds; omit for a point volume
blend_distance : distance over which the volume fades in, world units (default 10.0)
is_global      : True = affects entire scene regardless of camera position (default False)
priority       : override priority — higher wins when volumes overlap (default 0)
parent_path    : optional hierarchy parent path
name           : optional GameObject name

Responses
---------
overrides_applied : [str] — effect names that were successfully added and configured
overrides_failed  : [str] — "EffectName: reason" for any effect that failed
warnings          : [str] — per-property warnings (bad field name, type mismatch)

Example — dungeon entry atmosphere
------------------------------------
create_postprocessing_volume(
    profile_name="DungeonEntry",
    position=[0, 5, 0],
    size=[20, 10, 20],
    blend_distance=6.0,
    priority=1,
    overrides=[
        {"effect": "ColorAdjustments",
         "properties": {"saturation": -30.0, "postExposure": -0.5}},
        {"effect": "Bloom",
         "properties": {"intensity": 0.1, "threshold": 1.2}},
        {"effect": "Vignette",
         "properties": {"intensity": 0.4, "smoothness": 0.5}},
    ]
)

Example — global scene baseline
---------------------------------
create_postprocessing_volume(
    profile_name="SceneBase",
    is_global=True,
    priority=0,
    overrides=[
        {"effect": "Tonemapping",      "properties": {"mode": "ACES"}},
        {"effect": "ColorAdjustments", "properties": {"contrast": 8.0, "saturation": 5.0}},
        {"effect": "FilmGrain",        "properties": {"intensity": 0.12, "type": "Thin1"}},
    ]
)

tools.name: create_prefab_metadata
tools.summary: Create a PrefabMetadata ScriptableObject asset alongside a prefab.
tools.description:
Create a PrefabMetadata ScriptableObject asset alongside a prefab.

The asset is saved as Prefab_Name.metadata.asset in the same directory as
the prefab, following the project convention. After creation, MetadataRegistry
is reloaded so dress_area, resolve_scaffold_markers, and get_prefab_catalog
immediately reflect the new metadata.

The richer the metadata — especially description and tags — the better
the AI's placement and scoring decisions will be.

Parameters
----------
prefab_path         : AssetDatabase path, e.g. "Assets/Prefabs/Props/Barrel.prefab"
tags                : searchable tags, e.g. ["storage", "wooden", "breakable"]
description         : plain-English description including appearance, scale, and
                      ideal placement context. Be specific — this is read verbatim
                      by dress_area and resolve_scaffold_markers.
category            : broad category: "building", "prop", "vegetation",
                      "light-fixture", "terrain", etc.
display_name        : human-readable name shown in catalog and responses.
                      Defaults to the prefab filename if omitted.
compatible_with     : tags of other assets this pairs well with
incompatible_with   : tags this asset clashes with (agent avoids combining these)
requires_flat_ground: placement rule — must be placed on a flat surface (default True)
can_stack           : multiple instances may be stacked vertically (default False)
indoor_only         : only valid inside enclosed spaces (default False)
outdoor_only        : only valid in open outdoor areas (default False)
minimum_spacing     : minimum distance in metres between instances of this prefab
approximate_size    : bounding box [width, height, depth] in world units
overwrite           : replace existing metadata if one already exists (default False)

Returns
-------
{ prefab_path, metadata_path, created: true, overwritten: true|null }

Workflow
--------
# After a new prefab art drop:
get_prefab_catalog("Assets/Prefabs/Props/NewDrop")
# → lists prefabs with has_metadata: false
create_prefab_metadata(
    "Assets/Prefabs/Props/NewDrop/Barrel_Weathered.prefab",
    tags=["storage", "wooden", "weathered", "breakable"],
    description="A short weathered oak barrel. Suitable for taverns, docks, and storage yards. Pairs well with crates and rope coils.",
    category="prop",
    requires_flat_ground=True,
    minimum_spacing=0.3,
    approximate_size=[0.7, 0.9, 0.7]
)
# → metadata created, immediately available to dress_area

tools.name: update_prefab_metadata
tools.summary: Update specific fields on an existing PrefabMetadata asset.
tools.description:
Update specific fields on an existing PrefabMetadata asset.

Only the fields you provide are changed — omitted fields are left exactly
as they are on the existing asset. MetadataRegistry is reloaded after saving.

Use this to refine metadata iteratively:
  - Add tags after new context or biome requirements emerge
  - Improve descriptions as the art style solidifies
  - Adjust placement rules after testing in-engine
  - Add compatible_with / incompatible_with entries as relationships become clear

Parameters
----------
prefab_path  : AssetDatabase path used to locate the existing metadata asset
(all other parameters): see create_prefab_metadata — null = leave unchanged

Returns
-------
{ prefab_path, metadata_path, updated_fields: ["tags", "description", ...] }

Example — add tags and expand description
-----------------------------------------
update_prefab_metadata(
    "Assets/Prefabs/Props/Barrel_Weathered.prefab",
    tags=["storage", "wooden", "weathered", "breakable", "tavern", "dock"],
    compatible_with=["crate", "rope-coil", "lantern"]
)

tools.name: update_scene_context
tools.summary:
Write to the active SceneContext asset — the level design document that
Claude reads at the start of every session to guide placement decisions.
tools.description:
Write to the active SceneContext asset — the level design document that
Claude reads at the start of every session to guide placement decisions.

Only provided fields are changed. The updated asset is saved to disk immediately
so get_scene_context reflects the changes in the same session.

Tag parameters
--------------
active_tags        : full replacement (overwrites existing list)
add_active_tags    : append tags (ignored if active_tags is provided)
remove_active_tags : remove specific tags (ignored if active_tags is provided)
excluded_tags      : full replacement of the excluded list

Notes parameters
----------------
notes        : full replacement of the design notes field
append_notes : append to existing notes (ignored if notes is provided);
               adds a blank line separator before the new text

Returns
-------
{ context_path, updated_fields: ["active_tags", "notes", ...] }

Example — session notes workflow
---------------------------------
# At the end of a session, record what was done and what's still needed:
update_scene_context(
    add_active_tags=["ruined", "overgrown"],
    remove_active_tags=["pristine"],
    append_notes="2024-06-08: Added ruined east wing. "
                 "Avoid intact furniture in Zone3 eastward. "
                 "LOD groups still needed on Townhouse_C and WarehouseA."
)

tools.name: get_zone_context
tools.summary: Return the SceneContext for a specific scaffold zone.
tools.description:
Return the SceneContext for a specific scaffold zone.

Looks up the zone name in McpBridgeSettings.zoneContexts. If a matching
entry exists, returns that zone's dedicated context. If not, falls back
to the global SceneContext (same as get_scene_context).

Use this when working inside a named scaffold zone that has its own
design identity distinct from the rest of the scene — for example, a
'Forest_Ruins' zone in a tile that also contains a 'Village_Center' zone.

Parameters
----------
zone_name : name of the scaffold zone (must match a ScaffoldZone name and
            a ZoneContextEntry.zoneName in McpBridgeSettings exactly)

Returns
-------
Same shape as get_scene_context — level_name, setting, architectural_style,
era, active_tags, excluded_tags, notes — plus zone_name in the response
when a zone-specific context was found.

Workflow
--------
# Before dressing a zone with its own design identity:
get_zone_context("Zone3_Ruins")
# → returns ruined-specific active_tags even if the global context
#   is set to a broader 'medieval village' setting

tools.name: paint_terrain_layer
tools.summary: Paint a terrain texture layer at a world position using a circular brush.
tools.description:
Paint a terrain texture layer at a world position using a circular brush.

All layer weights are renormalised after painting so the alphamap sums to 1.0
at every affected pixel — you cannot end up with an invalid terrain.

Best used immediately after executing a dress_area proposal, to paint the
terrain layer that matches the placed props:
  - Place rocks and gravel → paint "RockyGround" under them
  - Place trees and undergrowth → paint "ForestFloor"
  - Dress a dirt path with weeds → paint "DirtPath" along the centre

Parameters
----------
position     : [x, y, z] world-space brush centre. Y is ignored for painting.
radius       : brush radius in world metres.
layer_name   : terrain layer to paint. Must match a layer name on the terrain
               tile (case-insensitive). If the name is wrong, the error response
               lists all available layer names.
opacity      : brush strength 0.0–1.0 (default 0.5). How strongly to paint
               at the brush centre.
falloff      : brush edge falloff.
               "smooth"   — S-curve ease-in/ease-out (default, most natural)
               "linear"   — even fade from centre to edge
               "constant" — full opacity everywhere inside the radius (hard edge)
blend_mode   : how opacity interacts with existing layer value.
               "add" — increase the layer toward opacity (default, safe for
                       layering multiple passes)
               "set" — force the layer to exactly opacity at the brush centre,
                       scaling all others down proportionally
terrain_name : name of the terrain tile to paint on. Omit to use the tile that
               covers position (correct for single-terrain scenes and most
               tiled setups).

Returns
-------
{ terrain_name, layer_painted, layer_index, pixels_affected, warnings }

Example — paint after dressing a forest clearing
-------------------------------------------------
# After executing a dress_area proposal for scattered trees and undergrowth:
paint_terrain_layer([60, 0, 40], radius=18,
                    layer_name="ForestFloor", opacity=0.7, blend_mode="set")
paint_terrain_layer([60, 0, 40], radius=22,
                    layer_name="Grass",       opacity=0.4, blend_mode="add")
# Centre is pure ForestFloor; outer ring blends back to Grass

tools.name: bake_lighting
tools.summary:
Start a background lighting bake (Unity's progressive lightmapper) and return
its job ID at once, or clear baked lighting data.
tools.description:
Start a background lighting bake (Unity's progressive lightmapper) and return
its job ID at once, or clear baked lighting data.

The lighting equivalent of bake_navmesh. Call at the end of any session
that makes significant geometry or lighting changes — new buildings, moved
lights, added prop clusters, or changed terrain.

Modes
-----
"async" (default)
    Starts the bake in the background and returns immediately with a
    job_id. The editor stays usable while it bakes. Bakes on large scenes
    take minutes: check progress and the result with
    get_job_status(job_id), stop the bake with cancel_job(job_id).

"clear"
    Deletes all baked lighting data from the scene without re-baking.
    Useful before a full rework of the lighting setup.

The old "sync" mode is refused: it froze the editor for the whole bake.

Parameters
----------
mode                   : "async" | "clear" (default "async")
bake_reflection_probes : Reflection probes set to Baked are captured by every
                         bake; True only mentions it in the result message.

Returns
-------
{ mode, started, job_id, message }
get_job_status(job_id) then reports { state, progress } while baking, and
{ state: "done", result: { completed, elapsed_ms, message } } at the end.

Example — end-of-session bake
------------------------------
# After a full dressing session:
bake_navmesh(all=True)    # NavMesh first — fast
bake_lighting(mode="async", bake_reflection_probes=True)
# → returns job_id; call get_job_status(job_id) later to confirm it finished

tools.name: replace_prefab
tools.summary:
Replace every instance of one prefab with another, preserving each
instance's transform, name, and hierarchy parent by default.
tools.description:
Replace every instance of one prefab with another, preserving each
instance's transform, name, and hierarchy parent by default.

All replacements are grouped under a single named Undo entry
("{old} → {new}"), so the entire operation can be reversed at once
with Cmd+Z in the Editor.

Only prefab instance roots are matched — children inside a prefab and
nested variant instances are not replaced individually.

Parameters
----------
old_prefab_path    : AssetDatabase path of the prefab being replaced
new_prefab_path    : AssetDatabase path of the replacement prefab
scope_path         : hierarchy path to restrict the search (default: whole scene)
preserve_transform : keep original position, rotation, and scale (default True)
preserve_name      : keep the instance's original GameObject name (default True)
preserve_parent    : keep the original hierarchy parent (default True)
dry_run            : return what would be replaced without modifying the scene

Returns
-------
{ replaced_count, dry_run, replaced: [{old_path, new_path}], warnings }

The new_path typically equals old_path when names are preserved — only the
underlying prefab asset changes.

Example — placeholder to final asset swap
------------------------------------------
# Art drop arrived — replace all placeholder houses
replace_prefab(
    old_prefab_path="Assets/Prefabs/Placeholders/House_Block.prefab",
    new_prefab_path="Assets/Prefabs/Buildings/Townhouse_A.prefab",
    scope_path="/World/Village",
    dry_run=True   # check count first
)
# → { replaced_count: 12, dry_run: True, ... }

replace_prefab(
    old_prefab_path="Assets/Prefabs/Placeholders/House_Block.prefab",
    new_prefab_path="Assets/Prefabs/Buildings/Townhouse_A.prefab",
    scope_path="/World/Village"
)
# → { replaced_count: 12, dry_run: False, ... }

tools.name: create_reflection_probe
tools.summary: Create a ReflectionProbe at a world position with a configurable influence volume.
tools.description:
Create a ReflectionProbe at a world position with a configurable influence volume.

In open-world levels, reflection probes are placed by the dozen — one per room,
one per archway, one per metallic or wet surface — always with the same setup.
This tool removes per-probe Inspector work.

After placing a batch of probes, trigger a lighting bake:
    bake_lighting(mode="async", bake_reflection_probes=True)

Parameters
----------
position   : [x, y, z] world-space centre of the probe and its influence box
size       : [w, h, d] extents of the influence volume in world units.
             Default [10, 5, 10]. The probe's influence is a box centred on position.
mode       : "baked"    — captures lighting at bake time (default; cheapest at runtime)
             "realtime" — re-captures every frame (expensive; use sparingly)
             "custom"   — uses a manually assigned cubemap texture
importance : priority when probe volumes overlap; higher wins. Default 1.
             Use 2+ for small interior probes that should override a larger outdoor probe.
intensity  : reflection intensity multiplier 0.0–1.0. Default 1.0.
hdr        : use HDR cubemap format. Default True.
resolution : cubemap capture resolution. Must be power of 2 from 16 to 2048.
             Default 128. Non-power-of-2 values are snapped to the nearest valid size.
             Guideline: 128 for typical rooms, 256 for large or visually prominent spaces,
             512+ only for hero shots.
parent_path: hierarchy path of a parent object
name       : GameObject name. Default "ReflectionProbe".

Returns
-------
{ object_path, mode, importance, size: [w,h,d], resolution }

Example — outfit a tavern interior
------------------------------------
create_reflection_probe(
    position=[8.0, 1.5, 14.0],
    size=[6.0, 3.5, 8.0],
    mode="baked",
    importance=2,
    resolution=256,
    parent_path="/World/Village/Tavern/Lighting",
    name="ReflectionProbe_TavernMain"
)
