tools.name: create_patrol_route
tools.summary: Create a named patrol route as a scene hierarchy structure.
tools.description:
Create a named patrol route as a scene hierarchy structure.

The route is created as:
    PatrolRoute_{name}/              ← container, PatrolRouteData component
        WP_00                        ← waypoint, PatrolWaypoint component
        WP_01_{label}                ← waypoint with label in its name
        ...

This structure is framework-agnostic. Your game's AI can discover routes at
runtime by finding GameObjects named "PatrolRoute_*" and reading child world
positions — no dependency on the bridge's editor-only components required.

The PatrolRouteData and PatrolWaypoint components carry design intent for the
editor session and are stripped from player builds. See PatrolRouteComponents.cs
for runtime integration options.

Parameters
----------
name              : route name, used as suffix on the container: "PatrolRoute_{name}"
waypoints         : ordered list of waypoint definitions. Each is a dict with:
                      position       [x, y, z] — required
                      idle_time      float      — seconds to idle here (-1 = use default)
                      look_direction [x, y, z]  — Euler angles to face while idling
                      label          str        — optional name suffix e.g. "east_gate"
loop              : True = last waypoint connects back to first (default True)
default_idle_time : seconds to idle at waypoints that don't specify their own (default 1.0)
zone_path         : hierarchy path of the ScaffoldZone to parent this route under.
                    Takes priority over parent_path. The zone must already exist.
parent_path       : fallback parent path when zone_path is not provided

Returns
-------
{ route_path, waypoint_count, loop, zone_path?, waypoints: [{path, label?}] }

Example — guard patrol in a dungeon antechamber
------------------------------------------------
create_patrol_route(
    name="GuardSweep_East",
    zone_path="/Dungeon/Zone2_Antechamber",
    loop=True,
    default_idle_time=1.5,
    waypoints=[
        {"position": [4.0, 0.0, 2.0],  "label": "entry_post",  "idle_time": 3.0},
        {"position": [12.0, 0.0, 2.0]},
        {"position": [12.0, 0.0, 14.0], "label": "far_corner",
         "idle_time": 2.0, "look_direction": [0, 90, 0]},
        {"position": [4.0, 0.0, 14.0]},
    ]
)

tools.name: get_patrol_routes
tools.summary: List all patrol routes currently in the active scene.
tools.description:
List all patrol routes currently in the active scene.

Returns each route with its waypoints, positions, idle times, labels, and
effective idle times (per-waypoint or resolved from the route default).

Use this before create_patrol_route to check what routes already exist in
a zone, or to review the current patrol layout before making changes.

Returns
-------
{ routes: [{ route_path, name, zone_path?, loop, waypoint_count,
             waypoints: [{ path, index, position, idle_time, label?, look_direction? }] }] }

tools.name: capture_scene_view
tools.summary: Render the active Unity Scene View and return the result as an image.
tools.description:
Render the active Unity Scene View and return the result as an image.

Claude receives the image directly in context and can describe what it
sees, identify layout issues, and suggest specific adjustments — closing
the visual feedback loop that otherwise requires manual viewport inspection
after every operation.

The capture renders the scene camera without editor gizmos and handles,
giving a clean view of the actual scene geometry. This is intentional:
the undecorated scene is what the player sees, and it is less cluttered
for spatial review than the gizmo-heavy editor view.

── TYPICAL USAGE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

After any placement or dressing operation:

    # Place props, then review
    execute_proposal("prop_dress_a3f2")
    capture_scene_view(focus_path="/World/Village/Market",
                       width=1920, height=1080)
    # Claude: "The north corner looks sparse — the stalls are clustered
    #          in the south. Should I scatter a few more crates at [22,0,18]?"

── PARAMETERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

width      : capture width in pixels (default 1280)
height     : capture height in pixels (default 720)
quality    : JPEG quality 1–100 (default 85).
             85 is a good balance of quality and response size.
             Use 60–70 for a quick overview; 95+ for detailed inspection.
focus_path : hierarchy path of an object to frame before capturing.
             The Scene View pivot and size are set from the object's
             renderer bounds. If the path is not found, the current
             view orientation is used and a warning is returned with
             the image.

── RETURN TYPE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Returns Image on success — Claude sees the scene image directly. When
Unity reports warnings (e.g. focus_path not found), they follow the
image as text.
Returns str on error — Claude sees the error message as text.

This is the only tool in the bridge that returns Image rather than a
JSON string. All other tools return json.dumps(result).

── REQUIREMENTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A Scene View window must be open and active in the Unity Editor.
The capture fails with NO_SCENE_VIEW if no Scene View is available
(e.g. if only the Game View is open, or Unity is minimised).

tools.name: write_project_file
tools.summary: Write a file to the Unity project's Assets folder. The file is not imported.
tools.description:
Write a file to the Unity project's Assets folder. The file is not imported.

    The most common use is creating new C# scripts, but it works for any text
    file: ScriptableObject data, shader graphs exported as JSON, config files,
    README documents, etc.

    Unity does not import the file and does not compile scripts until
    refresh_assets() is called (or the Unity Editor regains focus with Auto
    Refresh on). Write every file first, then call refresh_assets() once.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path               : path relative to Assets/, e.g. "Scripts/Player/PlayerController.cs"
                         A leading "Assets/" is accepted and stripped automatically.
    content            : full text content to write (UTF-8)
    overwrite          : replace the file if it already exists (default True).
                         Set False to protect existing files.
    create_directories : create intermediate directories if they don't exist (default True).
                         Set False to require the directory to exist first.

    Returns
    -------
    { asset_path, created: bool, overwrote: bool, bytes_written: int }

    Workflow — create a new MonoBehaviour
    -------------------------------------
    write_project_file(
        path="Scripts/AI/GuardPatrol.cs",
        content='''using UnityEngine;

public class GuardPatrol : MonoBehaviour
{
    public Transform[] waypoints;

    private void Start()
    {
    }
}'''
    )
    # Then, once all files are written: refresh_assets()

    Notes
    -----
    - Write all files first, send the final response, then call
      refresh_assets() to trigger compilation without killing the conversation.
    - Immediately after writing a script, wait for Unity to finish compiling
      before trying to add the new component to a scene object via add_component_to_object.
    - To update an existing script, call read_project_file first to see the
      current content, then write_project_file with the modified version.

tools.name: read_project_file
tools.summary: Read the text content of a file from the Unity project's Assets folder.
tools.description:
Read the text content of a file from the Unity project's Assets folder.

Use this to inspect an existing script before modifying it, to check whether
a file already exists before writing, or to read config and data files.

Parameters
----------
path : path relative to Assets/, e.g. "Scripts/Player/PlayerController.cs"
       A leading "Assets/" is accepted and stripped automatically.

Returns
-------
{ asset_path, exists: bool, content?: str, size_bytes?: int }

If the file does not exist, returns { exists: false } without an error —
use this to safely check for a file before writing it.

tools.name: list_project_files
tools.summary: List files in a directory under the Unity project's Assets folder.
tools.description:
List files in a directory under the Unity project's Assets folder.

.meta files are excluded from results automatically.

Parameters
----------
path      : directory path relative to Assets/ (empty = Assets root)
pattern   : file glob pattern (default "*"). Examples: "*.cs", "*.prefab", "*.asset"
recursive : include files in subdirectories (default False)

Returns
-------
{ directory, files: [str], count: int }

All returned paths are in "Assets/..." format.

Examples
--------
list_project_files("Scripts", "*.cs", recursive=True)
→ lists all C# scripts under Assets/Scripts/

list_project_files("Prefabs/Props", "*.prefab")
→ lists all prefabs directly in Assets/Prefabs/Props/

tools.name: refresh_assets
tools.summary:
Refresh the Unity AssetDatabase and trigger recompilation of any changed scripts.
Call it last: the recompile reloads Unity's scripts and can end the conversation.
tools.description:
Refresh the Unity AssetDatabase and trigger recompilation of any changed scripts.
Call it last: the recompile reloads Unity's scripts and can end the conversation.

Call this AFTER writing all files and AFTER composing the final response text —
not in the middle of a tool-call sequence. This avoids a domain reload killing
the in-flight conversation.

Correct workflow for creating a C# script:
    1. write_project_file(path="Scripts/Foo.cs", content="...")
    2. Compose and send your final summary response to the user
    3. [separately, if asked] call refresh_assets()

Or, if the user needs the script compiled as part of the same turn:
    1. write_project_file(...)
    2. refresh_assets()        ← this ends the agent turn (domain reload follows)
    3. (tell the user Unity is compiling)

Returns
-------
{ refreshed: true, message: str }
